name: 302 Wait Avenue Co-op
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: We are a cooperative living house on north campus that cares for one another and promotes a safe living space for women and non-binary identifying people.

name: 660 Stewart Cooperative
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, International/Multicultural, Sustainability/Environmental, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: The purpose of 660 shall be to provide quality housing, or rather a home to its members, by promoting the concept of cooperative living in accordance with the spirit of the Rochdale Principles of Cooperation.

name: Actuarial Society at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: Our club aims to provide awareness for the actuarial profession and to assist those striving to become an actuary by strengthening their leadership, networking, professional, and actuarial skills.

name: After Eight A Cappella
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: After Eight's purpose is to entertain audiences at Cornell and elsewhere while providing women and gender minorities the chance to perform contemporary music a cappella.

name: Agua Clara
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, Sustainability/Environmental
description: AguaClara Cornell is a student-led program that develops and implements sustainable, gravity-powered water treatment technologies to bring safe water on tap to communities around the world.

name: Air and Sea Hospitality
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: This organization explores the airline and cruise industry as a whole and exposes members to the various opportunities that exist within the businesses. We provide resources to help you learn more about the industry and build the knowledge and network to work in it.

name: ALANA Intercultural Programming Board
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, AY27 - Byline
description: We seek to provide the Cornell community with wide and diversified programming on a regular basis as well as allocate funds to registered student organizations for programs that encourage diversity and intercultural efforts.

name: Alpha Kappa Psi
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Professional Fraternity (PFC), PROF: Business and Management
description: Alpha Kappa Psi is Cornell University's Original Co-Ed Professional Business Fraternity dedicated to providing a professional and social environment in which its brothers can thrive. Founded in 1904, Alpha Kappa Psi is the nation's oldest professional business fraternity as well. Our chapter at Cornell University was founded in 1998 and is one of over 190 College Chapters across the nation, Canada, and the United Kingdom. We host and engage in a variety of professional, social, and philanthropic activities that help develop experienced and ethical leaders and foster life-long bonds and memories. Today, as always, the Omicron Upsilon chapter is dedicated to furthering the individual welfare of its members and the community.

name: Alzheimer's Buddies
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Alzheimer's Buddies at Cornell is a student-led organization aimed at overcoming the social disengagement experienced by those affected by intermediate-to-late-stages of Alzheimer's Disease. The purpose of this organization is to pair students to volunteer 1-on-1 with dementia residents, build social skills as well as raise awareness through participating in fundraisers and hosting talks on current advancements in Alzheimer's Disease research.

name: American Hotel and Lodging Association Student Chapter at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: The purpose of the chapter is to be the primary advocates of the American lodging industry for SHA students through education, information and member services, and to build meaningful and professional connections between the American Hotel and Lodging Association and Cornell University. Our main goals are as follows: 1.	To provide members opportunities to exchange ideas, strategies, and contacts with industry leaders at any of AH&LA events throughout the year. 2.	To educate members on the latest industry trend and research through AH&LA online information services. 3.	To expose new members to different aspects of hospitality business through hotel tours in New York City. 4.	To assist members to achieve their career goals through AH&LA's career services and network. 5.	To assist the local community through community service events. 6.	To provide our members with professional development opportunities with the help of fellow students, alumni, faculty, and industry professionals.

name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The primary vision of Cornell University's AISES chapter is the development of a new generation of educated Native leaders who will in turn contemplate, study, and contribute to the building of a Nation and community among Native Americans.

name: American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE) at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: We are Cornell's student chapter of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE), a national network of chemical engineering professionals and students.  Our chapter's mission is to strengthen the Cornell ChemE community and enrich the ChemE undergraduate experience through professional, outreach, and social programming.

name: American Meteorological Society at Cornell Chapter
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Sustainability/Environmental
description: We are Cornell Weather. Our mission is to encourage the pursuit of meteorological knowledge on Cornell's campus and create a community within the Atmospheric Science department. We also seek to introduce undergraduates to various professional opportunities in the Atmospheric Sciences and facilitate research, and help them work on skills crucial to the science in ways that help the Cornell community at large.

name: American Society of Mechanical Engineers at Cornell University Chapter
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: Cornell ASME aims to enrich the lives of students of the Sibley School by providing professional and social networking events, information about post-graduation career paths, and local outreach activities. We uphold the ASME mission to serve diverse global communities by advancing, disseminating and applying engineering knowledge for improving the quality of life, and communicating the excitement of engineering.

name: Animal Science: Mentoring Our Undergraduates
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: The mission of Animal Science: Mentoring Our Undergraduates is to foster mentorship between current Animal Science students and incoming Animal Science students with hopes to ease the transition into the program and build a community of students that spans generations.

name: AppDev at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team
description: The philosophy of Cornell AppDev is to curate a tight-knit, inclusive community where any person can be part of the process to solve problems through app development. We do this by building apps using industry-level techniques with an emphasis on mobile development, cultivating a strong mentorship culture, and educating the next generation of Cornellians in our craft.

name: Applied & Engineering Physics Society
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of this organization is to develop a strong and welcoming undergraduate culture in the Applied & Engineering Physics department. This group will create an infrastructure for undergraduates interested in or affiliated with A&EP to both act as and seek academic mentors, spend more time with A&EP peers in a social setting, participate in outreach events to encourage undergraduates to join the A&EP major, and to facilitate communication between the undergraduate community and the A&EP department faculty. The A&EP Society intends additionally to provide opportunities for members to explore the applications of studying A&EP outside of the theoretical knowledge gained in the classroom.

name: Aprendizaje Liderazgo Motivacion Autoestima
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural
description: ALMA exists to:  Build community among Latina and non-binary identifying students.  Provide professional and personal development through mentorship, networking, and leadership opportunities.  Coordinate and host events, social convenings, and cultural programming as voted and approved by the ALMA board via quorum.  Advocate for and amplify the voices of Latina and non-binary students across campus.

name: Army ROTC Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The Army ROTC Club at Cornell University provides leadership development within the framework of the Army Values, while promoting Equality, Fraternity, and Liberty within Cornell Leadership development efforts. In addition, the Army ROTC Club will impart education and outreach regarding Cornell's military history and achievements.

name: Art Beyond Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Visual Arts
description: Art Beyond Cornell aims to bring new perspectives to both Cornell students and institutionalized youth in the Tompkins County area by providing a means of connection, self-expression, communication, growth, and joy through art.

name: ASL @ Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: ASL @ Cornell aims to promote heightened awareness of and appreciation for American Sign Language (ASL) and Deaf culture in collaboration with Cornell’s ASL/Deaf Studies program. In doing so, we hope to cultivate an inclusive environment on campus and in the city of Ithaca that welcomes Deaf and hard of hearing individuals while allowing all students to develop a greater understanding of ASL and encouraging them to apply their classroom knowledge to the community.

name: Association for Engagement and Partnership
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The mission of the Association for Students and Community is to increase the recruitment and retention of students within the College of Human Ecology.

name: Association of Computer Science Undergraduates
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: The Association of Computer Science Undergraduates (ACSU) promotes educational, professional, and social interaction among every undergraduate student interested in computer science.

name: AutoBoat at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: Cornell AutoBoat aims to push the boundaries of novel maritime technology by designing, manufacturing, and testing an autonomous boat capable of image recognition, complex path planning, and interacting with its environment.

name: Autonomous Sailboat Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: The goal of CUSail is to design and manufacture a small, cheap, and mass-producible autonomous robotic sailboat that can intelligently navigate any body of water and collect data. The project is meant to decrease environmental research and acoustic marine mammal monitoring costs by designing a research vessel that can cheaply collect data.

name: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: The Cornell University Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (CUAUV) team designs and builds AUVs for competition and research. CUAUV competes annually in the RoboSub Competition, hosted by the AUVSI Foundation and Office of Naval Research in San Diego, California.

name: Baja Racing at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of Cornell Baja Racing shall be to design and build an off-road vehicle each year to compete in the Baja SAE Collegiate Design Series competition. The organization provides hands-on engineering, teamwork, and leadership experience to its diverse members from all backgrounds.

name: Best Buddies at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Best Buddies is a nonprofit organization dedicated to establishing a global volunteer movement that creates opportunities for one-to-one friendships, integrated employment, and leadership development for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD).

name: Big Red Ambassadors
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: Big Red Ambassadors is a university club in which Cornell students, under the guidance of the Undergraduate Admissions Office work as liaisons between current students and prospective students. Big Red Ambassadors participate in University information sessions, responding to general student-life questions emailed to admissions, lead our Cornell Days program (a special on-campus program for admitted students), and in general, are a primary resource for prospective students and their families.

name: Big Red Bears
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: A student organization aimed to increase school spirit through the use of the Cornell mascot, Touchdown the Big Red Bear. We work to bring Touchdown to every Cornell athletic event and every university event for which we are requested, along with certain requested private events. We also train new students to become Touchdown and ensure that his legacy and spirit can continue to be passed on to Cornellians past, present, and future.

name: Big Red Buddies
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: Our mission is to engage interested Cornell undergraduates with the Ithaca community by providing weekly volunteering opportunities at the Head Start Centers in Ithaca.  Our focus is on emphasizing the importance of early childhood development and allowing Cornell students to use their skills to foster relationships with the younger students of our community, with a focus on working with underserved children.

name: Big Red Marching Band
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The objective of the BRMB is to foster an inclusive and open environment where all band members feel welcome and comfortable regardless of any identity a member may hold. The primary functions of the Big Red Bands are to promote school spirit, support the activities of Cornell athletics, and provide musical and visual entertainment to the Ithaca community.

name: Big Red Pep Band at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The purpose of the Big Red Pep Band is to provide musical entertainment and promote school spirit at Cornell and elsewhere. The Pep Band is responsible for attending all Men's home hockey games while classes are in session, along with as many other athletic contests as possible.

name: BigRed/Hacks
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: BigRed//Hacks is Cornell's collegiate hackathon. During the academic year, we also hold workshops and events for the Cornell community.

name: Biomedical Device at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: Biomedical Device at Cornell (CUBMD) is a team of multidisciplinary undergraduate students formed under a shared interest for biomedical device innovation with the ultimate goal of advancing healthcare. Our mission is to identify contemporary problems in the field of biomedical devices, design and innovate solutions to said problems, and work to bring our solutions to the market where they can have the most widespread, positive impact.

name: Black Bio-medical and Technical Association
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: This organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University. BBMTA of Cornell University is a non-profit organization dedicated to serving underrepresented students interested in pursuing health-related careers. The organization provides underrepresented students with a community and resources to succeed as pre-health undergraduate students. BBMTA hosts general body meetings where students obtain academic support, professional development skills and awareness of health-related issues. Through our annual health career conference composed of panels and workshops, we expose students to a range of health professionals and give students the opportunity to engage with those already established in the medical field. BBMTA extends its mission into the Ithaca community beyond Cornell through commitment to various service projects and youth mentorship.

name: Black Students United
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: BSU is an agent of service to the people of the Pan-African Diaspora at Cornell; this is accomplished by addressing their political, organizational, institutional, social, and educational needs. This organization was established as a comprehensive alliance with a focus on resource organization and implementation. It provides a network/space for the members of the Pan-African Diaspora to express their needs and have those needs met. BSU is committed to Afro-centricity, occupying the nexus of academia & activism, and developing community-centered leadership. It is committed to Pan-African unity across lines of ethnicity, culture, socio-economic class, sex, gender, sexual orientation, and religion.

name: Block and Bridle Club at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife
description: CU Block and Bridle is the Cornell branch of a national club with collegiate students interested in working with livestock, gaining animal experience, and spreading animal science and agricultural knowledge to the Cornell and Greater Ithaca community. Each year we feature guest speakers chosen by club interest, social activities including organic farm tours and apple picking, and hands-on animal activities including a student organized Livestock Show.

name: Building Ourselves Through Sisterhood and Service Peer Mentorship Program
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Building Ourselves through Sisterhood and Service (B.O.S.S.) aims to foster healthy and genuine relationships between upperclassmen and underclassmen womxn of color, promote positive social interactions within womxn of color communities, encourage high academic and personal standards, provide access to helpful campus resources, and inspire community involvement and commitment to service. Incoming freshmen are paired with juniors. These pairs will stay together formally for 1 year. Although the program understands the importance of the year for growth and development, matches of sophomores and seniors can be made on a case-by-case basis. For example, a sophomore transfer student may be matched with a senior. We create a variety of programs throughout the year that encourage pairs to bond as well as serve the Cornell and Ithaca community.

name: ChemE Car at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of Cornell ChemE Car is threefold. The first purpose is to design and build a shoe box-sized car that is powered and stopped via chemical reactions. The second purpose is to provide students with the opportunity to apply engineering knowledge and skills. The third purpose is to contribute to the development of Chemical Engineering at Cornell University through attendance at regional and national competitions, research and development, and student-driven innovation.

name: Chorus at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The purposes of the Chorus are the study, practice, performance, and promotion of choral music at the university, within the Ithaca community, and beyond.

name: Cinema Student Advisory Board at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts, Visual Arts
description: The Cornell Cinema Student Advisory Board is an organization of students, both undergraduate and graduate, whose purpose is to represent and promote Cornell Cinema, as well as to advise and assist Cornell Cinema in its overall mission to offer the Cornell and greater Ithaca community a wide variety of cinematic and media experiences, for both educational and entertainment purposes.

name: Classics Society at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural
description: The Classics Society shall be to foster an appreciation of the study of ancient Greece and Rome, by looking to its languages, philosophies, archaeology, art, history, literature, and cultures to inform our contemporary world.

name: Club Sports Council
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: CSC allocates funds to nearly 70 undergraduate student organizations. Our mission is to support club sport teams in their ability to foster community and belonging at Cornell through funding opportunities.

name: Combat Robotics at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: The mission of Combat Robotics @ Cornell (CRC) is to inspire students both inside and outside of engineering to develop skills and gain experience in the exciting field of combat robotics. We strive to create a community where above all, learning is encouraged and members are willing and able to contribute to the best of their abilities, whether it be through helping to build the robot, organizing logistics for competition, securing sponsorships and grants from companies, or working to maintain the team's public image through the team's website and social media accounts. Our organization aims to provide an environment where members can learn from and teach one another. The mechanical members will learn the fundamentals of robot design, while firmware members learn how to integrate automation into combat robotics. Our marketing members will improve their networking and marketing skills to develop our team's reputation at Cornell. Beyond technical skills, we seek to promote soft skills such as teamwork, accountability, and time management in order to prepare students for leadership roles in their future professional and personal lives.

name: Community Elderly Partnership at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The mission of Community Elderly Partnership at Cornell (CEP) is to reduce social isolation and improve the quality of life for residents of nursing homes in the Ithaca community. CEP aims to achieve this mission by visiting local nursing homes every week in order to foster relationships and mutual learning amongst its members and the residents. Additionally, CEP strives to promote intergenerational awareness of the issues that face the elderly in today’s society. https://tinyurl.com/Officer-Responsibilites

name: Community Partnership Funding Board
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The Community Partnership Funding Board (CPFB), is a student-run board that seeks to foster student leadership and social responsibility by encouraging students to take action against social problems.  The CPFB assists students in developing grassroots community action projects and administers grants made possible by the Student Activities Fee via the Student Assembly.

name: Compass: The Cornell & George Junior Republic Partnership
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Our organization functions in association with and with support from the Einhorn Center for Community Engagement and the George Junior Republic High School (GJR). Our objectives are: 1.	To centralize the needs and interests of the GJR students in the development and maintenance of quality after-school programming 2.	To critically reflect on off-campus civic engagement and the larger systems in which we enact such engagement 3.	To nourish a reciprocal partnership in which Cornell students both provide resources for and learn from GJR students 4.	To provide support and opportunities for personal reflection to all Compass members 5.	To serve as a gatekeeper to the GJR after-school programs and provide support for other students, classes, or professors who may wish to engage with Compass organizations 6.	To coordinate and maintain strong communication channels with GJR teachers program co-facilitators (i.e. the Math and Literacy Coaches) 7.	To provide educational opportunities for the Cornell community, and especially Compass members, on broader systems of oppression – such as socioeconomic status, racial identity, gender identity, sexuality, ability status, etc. – that contribute to the disenfranchisement of many of the GJR students 8.	To counteract that disenfranchisement and empower GJR students by providing them a platform for creativity, learning, and leadership

name: Concrete Canoe at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: Our team’s mission is to collaboratively engineer the most strong, lightweight canoe possible out of concrete mixtures. We present our work in the spring ASCE Regional Concrete Canoe Competition through a presentation and a race, displaying our innovative new concrete mix and molding techniques.

name: Convocation Committee
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: Create an experience that embodies our class that stays with students for a lifetime.

name: Cornell Asian Pacific Student Union
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AY27 - Byline
description: The Cornell Asian Pacific-Islander Student Union is the umbrella organization for Asian/Asian-American and Asian-interest organizations at Cornell University. We aim to bring undergraduate organizations representing students of Asian descent together to facilitate networking among the members of the community. We strive to be the platform for the Cornell community to learn about and understand our diverse ethnic backgrounds in order to form a more cohesive community.

name: Cornell Assistive Technologies Project Team
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, AFFILIATION: Project Team
description: The mission of the Cornell Assistive Technologies Project Team is to champion inclusivity by developing assistive technologies for people with disabilities and to raise awareness about the impact of adapted solutions and assistive technologies among youths and communities in Ithaca and beyond.

name: Cornell Business Analytics Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: Cornell Business Analytics Club is a student-run organization that offers pro-bono business analytics consulting services to clients, both on and off campus. Our motto stems from the idea that data-driven decision making is a key to successful businesses and organizations.

name: Cornell CMSX
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: To maintain and build on CMSX, a course management system used by Cornell's faculty and students to aid the daily administration of classes.

name: Cornell Concert Commission
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts, Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: The purpose of Cornell Concert Commission shall be to provide the Cornell community with popular and diverse, contemporary musical entertainment which is both financially sound and responsive to the community's needs and desires.

name: Cornell Cup Robotics
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: The mission of this team is to provide a valuable, practical experience for students with robotics and embedded systems, and to demonstrate the extraordinary technology that we are able to create.

name: Cornell Current Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: Cornell Current is Cornell University's first current events and industry trends organization created to provide Cornell students a forum to proactively analyze the global and industry trends that are shaping our world today. Our members are not looking to simply discuss current events and industry trends as it pertains to the facts of what happened. We are highly interested in analysis of these trends: the why, the cause and effect, the bigger ramifications, and data-driven forward outlook to where trends could end up.

name: Cornell Dance Team
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive
description: We are the Cornell University Dance Team! Since our establishment in 2017, we have been sharing our love of dance both on campus and with the community.

name: Cornell Fashion Collective
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, Visual Arts
description: The Cornell Fashion Collective, formerly the Cornell Design League, is a student-run organization that provides members of the Cornell community with an outlet to express creativity in fashion and fashion management. Each spring, our organization presents a professional runway show featuring the talent of students who both design apparel and manage the operations of the show. Our organization gives students the opportunity to practice design, demonstrate their talents, and learn how to produce a large-scale fashion event.

name: Cornell Fashion Industry Network
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: The purpose of CFIN shall be to serve as Cornell's direct link to the fashion industry by facilitating relationships between students and alumni as well as teaching tangible networking and professional skills.

name: Cornell Hunger Relief Program
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: Cornell Hunger Relief Program works to learn about local and global food systems and to address hunger issues in Ithaca and Tompkins County by facilitating food drives to benefit local food pantries.

name: Cornell Hyperloop Project Team
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of Cornell Hyperloop shall be to bring the concept of Hyperloop to life, spearhead the development of Hyperloop technology, and show the world that Hyperloop is the next breakthrough in the transportation industry.

name: Cornell Livestock Judging Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife
description: Students will evaluate beef cattle, pigs, sheep, and goats from both a phenotypic and genotypic standpoint to determine the potential productivity and value of livestock within their respective segments of the industry. Students will understand how different physical traits are prioritized based on the function of each species and sex class, including how value is determined from meat and carcass evaluation. Pedigree and other genetic data will also be analyzed to accompany live evaluation and infer the potential merit of individual livestock as pieces in a breeding system. Lastly, students will also create and deliver oral reasons to support and validate their evaluation of livestock.

name: Cornell Real Estate Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: The Real Estate Club at Cornell provides educational, professional, and networking opportunities that enable students to succeed in their real estate endeavors. CREC leverages the University's unparalleled resources in business, hospitality, law, architecture, urban planning, public policy, and sustainability to develop well-informed professionals who understand the complexity of today's real estate industry.  CREC collaborates with the Center for Real Estate and Finance, Cornell Real Estate Council, and the Associate Real Estate Council (AREC-the graduate student real estate council) to provide the latest industry tools and resources for its members.

name: Cornell Seismic Design Project Team
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of this organization is to give students hand-on experience in seismic design while building structures to compete with other colleges and universities across the country. Students will use computer softwares, learn about design and seismology, and review the litigation codes for competition provided by the EERI Student Leadership Council.

name: Cornell Students Create Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The mission of Cornell Students Create is to connect students from across the university to the the Department of Performing and Media Arts and to promote student engagement in the performing and media arts in general on campus.

name: Cornell University Cheerleading
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: Our purpose is to generate school spirit at athletic events and to represent Cornell University at cheerleading and other sporting events by performing at competitions and exhibitions.

name: Cornell University Chorale
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: ​The mission of the Chorale is “the practice and performance of choral music for all voices with no restriction on experience or knowledge.”

name: Cornell University Class Councils
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: The Cornell University Class Councils will serve as a community-building organization focused on fostering a sense of unity and pride among the four University's undergraduate classes and varied student communities. We aim to prioritize our relationship with other student organizations and use our resources to plan class events, collaborate with other student groups, and establish and execute traditions. The Class Councils shall also strengthen student ties to the University by providing services to Cornell students before and after graduation.

name: Cornell University Diversity Admissions Ambassadors
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: We are an organization built for and by students. The Cornell University Admissions Ambassadors (CUDAA) partner and collaborate with staff in the Undergraduate Admissions Office (UAO) Admissions and partners in admissions and higher education in general including college access organizations nationwide to either, expose, introduce, or explain the Cornell or college student experience to prospective students, especially historically underrepresented students (including African American, Latino/a, First Americans (Native- American), Pacific Islander, bi-racial/multi-ethnic/multi-lingual, multi-abled, First-generation, Rural, Transfers, Veteran, etc.). CUDAA accomplishes these goals by coordinating and participating in volunteer recruitment activities including, but not limited to, recruit-a-thons, student hosting, high school / community-based organization (CBO) in-person (on campus) visits, virtual visits, virtual outreach programming, campus discussions, strong partnerships, strategic operations, and community outreach. CUDAA actively seeks opportunities to collaborate with other students, offices, and organizations committed to the recruitment, recognition, celebration, and retention of a talented and diverse student body. Through the collective, organized efforts of students, faculty, and staff on campus. CUDAA strives to perfect Ezra Cornell's founding vision to create "an institution where any person can find instruction in any study."

name: Cornell Votes
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Political/Speech/Debate
description: Through non-partisanship, Cornell Votes strives to institutionalize and create a campus culture in which every person exercises their right to have a voice in their representation through voting, democratic engagement, and civic discourse within the Cornell University ecosystem.

name: Cornell XR
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming, Gaming/Esports
description: The purpose of Cornell XR Project Team shall be to create a community of students developing projects such as apps, hardware, and games within the field of Virtual, Augmented, Mixed Reality (XR) and Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) for societal good and to enable students to interact with these innovative fields.

name: CU Autonomous Drone
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming

name: Custom Silicon Systems at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: Silicon CMOS chips are at the heart of every modern computing device from the smallest Internet-of Things (IoT) device to the largest supercomputer. Unfortunately, undergraduate students currently do not have any opportunity to actually go through the process of fully specifying, designing, implementing, testing, fabricating, and evaluating a computer chip. Undergraduates leave Cornell thinking that fabricating computer chips is only possible at huge companies like Intel, AMD, NVIDIA and Apple. Until recently, there was no realistic hands-on way for students to, experience the complete computer chip design process. At the same time, exposing students to the beauty of computer chip design has never been more important, since the slowing of CMOS technology scaling means computer system designers must increasingly rely on specialized computer chips for continued improvements in performance and/or energy efficiency. How can students (from freshmen to seniors) gain hands-on computer chip design experience? The answer lies in the recent explosion in open-source chip design tools, open-source chip implementations, open-source process design kits, and low-cost computer chip fabrication services. Just as open-source software has democratized software design, open-source hardware is poised to democratized hardware design. In addition to open source hardware, changes in IP control regulations have enabled students to utilize older, commercial design kits. Universities are also uniquely poised to access cutting-edge commercial design tools, enabling student-led designs to be made with these ever more accessible design kits. Due to a combination of both the accessibility of open-source, and the power of industry tools, IC design has never before been so available to interested undergraduates. The Cornell Custom Silicon Systems (C2S2) Project Team is a new project team traditionally funded through the Shen Fund for Social Impact, as well as commercial (AMD, Cadence, Marvell, Amazon Annapurna Labs) and government (Sandia National Labs, NORDTECH) sponsorships. The team is leveraging this emerging open and closed-source hardware ecosystems to enable undergraduate students to specify, design, implement, test, fabricate, and evaluate custom computer chips. The final outcome will be a custom computer chip integrated on a custom circuit board with a complete software stack targeting an important application domain. This ambitious student-led team is likely unique across US universities, and will hopefully inspire a new generation of computer system designers.

Working together with other emergency services from Cornell University and Tompkins County, CUEMS provides a valuable resource to the Ithaca campus and much of the surrounding Tompkins County community.

description: Hotel Ezra Cornell (HEC) is a weekend-long business conference organized and executed by the students of the School of Hotel Administration. The conference boasts a series of educational seminars, food and beverage events, and leisure activities to generate thought-provoking conversation about the industry and build long-term relationships between current and future hospitality professionals. description: The self-governing body for the 33 recognized Interfraternity Council fraternities at Cornell.  Creates policies, oversees the judicial process, and plans programming and initiatives for the community.  Has a 9 person elected IFC Exec Board.

name: International Students Association
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, AY27 - Byline
description: The recently rechristened International Students Association (ISA), previously the International Students Union (ISU) and International Students Board (ISB) is an organization of students from a diverse background committed to promoting dialogue and awareness about world events, cultures and issues. We fulfill this goal through the ISA's original events and the funding of student organizations, as well as assisting in the planning and execution of their events. The ISA believes that the university environment offers a unique opportunity for the interaction of ideas and opinions. The prestige and resources of Cornell University allow us to plan major events and to hear from influential speakers, and we are committed to fulfilling this potential. Further, the ISA encourages all student groups to approach the Board with ideas and suggestions concerning events or speakers they would like to see on campus. The International Students Association is also committed to student advocacy, focusing on issues that affect international and diverse students. These projects can be in response to long-term concerns, current global events, or changes in policies by the university's administration. While many members of the organization participate in department jazz ensembles, JazzPlus is open to everyone. JazzPlus presents workshops and clinics to musicians and listeners of the Cornell and Ithaca communities. Topics of discussion may include but are not limited to: jazz style, technique, composition, fundamentals, improvisation, history, culture, and performance. JazzPlus will sponsor a lecture series with guest artists from outside of the area as well as from the local community. JazzPlus will also facilitate musical events to provide the Cornell and surrounding communities with the opportunity to appreciate jazz by participating as performers and as spectators. Events may include but are not limited to: regular jazz-related social events, jam sessions and concerts on campus, publicizing JazzPlus and Cornell University Jazz Ensemble performances, and promotion of other jazz events on and off campus.

name: La Asociación Latina

name: Language Expansion Program
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Through weekly peer-led Language Corners, the Language Expansion Program provides a cooperative and encouraging environment for students to practice their target languages and exchange cultural knowledge. We foster language proficiency and cultural empathy within the Cornell community, with the goal that members will better serve their communities through translation and interpreting.

name: Liquid Propulsion at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: Our goal is to help Cornell students develop relevant skills and expertise in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, and Business Operations through our team’s technical projects focused on experimental rocket and jet propulsion research and development.

name: Logos: The Cornell Undergraduate Philosophy Club and Journal
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Publication/Media, Political/Speech/Debate
description: Logos: The Cornell Undergraduate Philosophy Club and Journal is a refereed journal at the Sage School of Philosophy in Ithaca, New York. An entirely student-run journal, Logos publishes undergraduate work in all branches and traditions of philosophy. Undergraduates from around the globe are invited to submit papers annually for peer-review. Accepted papers are published in the current year's edition of Logos, and the authors of the top three submissions are awarded cash prizes. In addition to publishing the journal, Logos functions as the general-interest philosophical club for the undergraduate student body. Logos sponsors reading and discussion groups, lectures, debates, and social events. Students of all backgrounds are welcome and encouraged to join.

name: Mars Rover at Cornell

We work to reduce the stigma of mental illness by holding educational events and creating safe spaces to foster a healthy, balanced lifestyle. CMM acts as a liaison between students, faculty, staff, and administration to advocate for the student perspective on mental health resources and campus policies. Through our project teams and G-Body members, we continue to provide accessible resources that serve the needs of our diverse living-learning community. Whether your interests stem from personal experiences, academic goals, a desire for social action, or curiosity, we welcome you to join us on our mission. We all have mental health- spend your time at Cornell prioritizing yours! Cornell Minds Matter is a Student Assembly Byline Organization.

MILRSO maintains corporate and alumni contacts to aid members' professional development. For MILRSO, underrepresented identities include: people of color, the LGBTQ community, non-conforming persons, women, or gender. MILRSO exists as a place for these communities to feel welcome and to feel supported.
